name: EMSculpt muscle stimulation

card.summary: A clinic device that triggers intense muscle contractions with focused electromagnetic energy to tone muscle and, with the Neo version, add heat to reduce fat.
card.aka: EMSCULPT, EMSCULPT NEO, HIFEM, high-intensity focused electromagnetic therapy, BTL
card.note: Published studies are small and many are industry-linked; systematic reviews describe the evidence as limited.

quick.overview:
EMSCULPT, made by BTL Industries, uses high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) energy to cause supramaximal muscle contractions in the abdomen, buttocks and other areas. The aim is to increase muscle tone or mass. EMSCULPT NEO adds radiofrequency heating to also reduce fat.

Published studies include MRI and multi-center buttock studies, and systematic reviews that assess efficacy and safety of electromagnetic treatments for body contouring.
quick.mechanism: A magnetic field induces involuntary muscle contractions stronger than voluntary ones. The manufacturer and researchers report that this can thicken muscle and, in the NEO version, add radiofrequency heat to reduce fat.
quick.risks: The reviewed literature describes few adverse effects, but evidence is limited and the early studies are small. The EMSCULPT NEO device is described as FDA-cleared for muscle toning and fat reduction in a 2024 systematic review.

lead: EMSCULPT (BTL Industries) is a non-invasive body-contouring treatment that uses high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) energy to stimulate muscle contractions in areas such as the abdomen and buttocks. A 2024 systematic review describes EMSCULPT NEO as an FDA-cleared treatment for increasing muscle tone and reducing fat, in which HIFEM builds muscle mass and combined radiofrequency is intended to reduce fat [1].

Early studies include a 22-patient abdominal study evaluated with MRI that introduced HIFEM and established hypotheses for future research [2] and a multi-center study of 75 patients examining toning and lifting of gluteal muscles [3]. Systematic reviews of electromagnetic treatments for body contouring have since been published [4][1][5].
infobox: High-intensity focused electromagnetic energy (HIFEM); NEO adds radiofrequency [1]

paras: HIFEM technology induces muscle contractions that the first MRI study of the abdomen described as having a dual tissue effect, on both muscle and fat [2]. EMSCULPT NEO combines electromagnetic energy with radiofrequency, intended to build muscle mass while reducing fat [1].

In the abdominal study, 22 patients received four treatments and were evaluated with anthropometry, photographs and MRI [2]. A multi-center study of 75 patients aged 22 to 59 evaluated gluteal toning and lifting [3]. A 2023 systematic review in Annals of Plastic Surgery examined imaging measurements and safety of electromagnetic treatments for body contouring [4], and a 2024 systematic review addressed HIFEM with and without radiofrequency [1]. A 2025 review covers electromagnetic treatment plus radiofrequency [5]. Specific effect sizes are not detailed here.

Human studies include the MRI abdominal study [2], the gluteal multi-center study [3], and systematic reviews [4][1][5]. Two registered buttock-lifting trials with a magnetic device were withdrawn [6][7]. Other registered HIFEM trials concern back pain [8]. Many device studies are small and the reviews note the evidence base is still developing.

timeline.event: Multi-center HIFEM buttock toning and lifting study published [3].
MRI study of HIFEM abdominal body shaping published [2].
First systematic review of electromagnetic body-contouring treatments published [4].
Systematic review of HIFEM with and without radiofrequency published [1].
